q: 1. The proportion by which the actual size of an object is enlarged or reduced in drawing is simply known as
explain: This proportion, drawing size to actual size, is by definition called the scale of the drawing.

q: 2. The scale should never be used as a ......... for drawing straight lines.
explain: Using a measuring scale as a straight edge for drawing can damage its precision graduations; a dedicated straight edge should be used instead.

q: 3. Site plan shows
explain: A site plan is a plan view of the plot showing the location and orientation of the building(s) on the site along with surrounding features such as roads and boundaries.

q: 4. Scales for architectural and building drawings for plan is generally taken as .............
explain: Building plans are conventionally drawn at a scale of 1:100, which balances readable detail with manageable sheet size for typical buildings.

q: 5. The shape of scales are
explain: Drafting scales are commonly manufactured in flat shapes for portability or triangular shapes to provide multiple scale ratios on a single instrument.

q: 6. The drawing for municipality is done at scale
explain: Municipal drawings often use 1:100 (metric) or 1" = 8' (FPS) as standard scales for site plans and building layouts to ensure clarity for legal approvals.

q: 7. To measure a fraction we use
explain: A diagonal scale is used to represent three consecutive units (e.g., meters, decimeters, and centimeters) and can measure very small fractions of a unit.

q: 8. Find the RF for scale 1cm = 25 km
explain: RF = Drawing Distance / Actual Distance. $1\text{ cm} / (25 \times 1000 \times 100)\text{ cm} = 1 / 2,500,000$.

q: 9. An engineer's scale would be used to measure lines on a drawing where the scale factor reads
explain: An engineer's scale is graduated in decimal (engineering) units such as 1 inch = 100 feet, unlike an architect's scale which uses fractional feet-inch scales.

q: 10. When a drawing is made to the same size of the object, the name of the scale is .............
explain: A scale with representative fraction 1:1, where the drawing size equals the actual object size, is called a full-size (natural) scale.

q: 11. To draw small objects, the scale used is .............
explain: Very small objects (e.g., watch parts) need to be drawn larger than actual size for clarity, requiring an enlarging (enlarged) scale.

q: 12. Site plans usually show the extent of .............
explain: A site plan's primary purpose is to show the extent (boundaries and layout) of the building site/plot itself, along with the position of structures on it.

q: 13. The ratio of distance on the drawing sheet and corresponding actual distance of the object is known as .............
explain: The Representative Factor (R.F.) is defined as the ratio of the length of a line on the drawing to the corresponding actual length on the object, expressed in the same units.

q: 14. When a drawing is made to the same size of the object, the name of the scale is
explain: A scale of 1:1, where drawing size equals actual size, is called full size scale.

q: 15. The drawing scale of 1 : 25 are best used in .............
explain: A scale of 1:25 provides enough detail for showing reinforcement bar layout in structural/RCC drawings, which require clarity finer than a general building plan scale.

q: 16. The ratio of the length on the drawing to the actual length know as
explain: This ratio is formally termed the Representative Factor (RF) of the drawing.

q: 17. Representative fraction when making a drawing in scale of 1 cm =10m will be:
explain: 1 cm = 10 m = 1000 cm, so the RF is 1:1000.

q: 18. Drawing made to one half of the actual size is
explain: A scale of 1:2 means the drawing is exactly half the size of the actual object.

q: 19. The maps which are on sufficiently large scale to enable the individual features shown on the map to be identified on the ground by their shape and position are called:
explain: A large-scale site plan shows enough detail that individual features can be identified on the ground by their shape and position.

q: 20. For drawing of small objects, the scale used is
explain: Small objects like watch parts are drawn using an enlarged scale (e.g., 5:1) so that details are visible.

q: 21. Scales usually used in civil engineering drawings are
explain: Because civil structures are large, they are almost always drawn to a reduced scale so they fit on standard sheets.

q: 22. Diagonal Scales are used for measurement of
explain: A diagonal scale can measure three successive units (e.g., metres, decimetres, centimetres) using its diagonal subdivisions.

q: 23. Site plan is a .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'structural plan' is marked as the answer for this item, categorizing the site plan under the structural drawing set in this reference's classification.

q: 24. The proportion by which the actual size of an object is enlarged or reduced in drawing is simply known as
explain: Scale is the ratio of the drawing size to the real-world size.

q: 25. When measurements are required in three consecutive units, the appropriate scale is .............
explain: A diagonal scale allows measurement of three successive units (e.g., meters, decimeters, centimeters) using the principle of similar triangles, unlike a plain scale which reads only two units.

q: 26. In the diagonal scale, the word "diagonal" is used because it is most suitable for the measurement of .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'all of these' is marked correct; more precisely, the term 'diagonal scale' actually derives from the diagonal lines drawn within its construction (used to subdivide the smallest unit), not from measuring diagonals of shapes directly, but the reference selects option (d).

q: 27. Scale used for the building drawing for municipal approval is
explain: Municipal building-permit drawings are conventionally submitted at a scale of 1:100.

q: 28. The purpose of an isometric scale is .............
options: to project the object on projection plane
explain: An isometric scale is specifically constructed to convert true lengths into isometric (foreshortened) lengths, so that isometric drawings can be plotted directly using foreshortened measurements.

q: 29. Find the RF for scale 1 cm = 2.5km
explain: 1 cm = 2.5 km = 250,000 cm, so the Representative Factor is 1:250,000.

q: 30. Scale:
explain: As given in the answer key, this option corresponds to the correct scale statement among those listed.

q: 31. The maps which are on sufficient large scale to enable the individual features shown on the map to be identified on the ground by their shape and position are called :
explain: Topographical maps use a large scale to represent both natural and man-made features of the terrain in detail.

q: 32. When 1 cm on a map represents 100 m on the ground, then the scale of the drawing is
explain: 1 cm = 100 m = 10,000 cm, so the scale is 1:10,000.

q: 33. Which of the following scales is not found in a standard set of drawing scale tools?
explain: Standard architect/engineer scale sets commonly include ratios such as 1:2, 1:5, and 1:10 (multiples of 2 and 5), but 1:3 is not a standard scale typically included in such sets.

q: 34. Which of the following scales is not found in a standard set of drawing scale tools?
explain: Standard scale sets typically include ratios like 1:2, 1:5 and 1:10; 1:3 is not a conventional standard scale.

q: 35. Scale used for two system of units measurement is .............
explain: A comparative scale is specifically designed to show corresponding measurements in two different systems of units (e.g., miles and kilometers) on the same scale.

q: 36. Diagonal of a square can be measured by a .............
explain: Since a plain, diagonal, or vernier scale can each be used to measure a linear length (such as the diagonal of a square, once calculated), all of these scale types are applicable for reading off that length.

q: 37. For common residential building permits from the municipalities, which is the mostly used b scale for preparation of site plans?
explain: A scale of 1:100 is the commonly used scale for site plans submitted for residential building permits.

q: 38. Which of the following regarding scales in drawing is NOT true?
options: the name of the scale (e.g. scale 1:10) should be mentioned below the scale
a diagonal scale consists of a primary scale and a venirer
comparative scales may be plain or diagonal
when an unusual scale is used it is constructed on the drawing sheet
explain: A diagonal scale is used to read three dimensions (e.g., meters, decimeters, centimeters) but does not technically use a 'vernier' like a vernier scale does.

q: 39. Site plan is a :
explain: A site plan is an architectural document that shows the footprint of a building and its relationship to the property lines.

q: 40. The ratio of the length of the drawing to the actual length of the object is called.
explain: This ratio is formally called the representative fraction of the drawing.

q: 41. *The space covered by a drawing in a paper after changing the scale from 1:100 to 1:50 will:
explain: Moving from 1:100 to 1:50 makes the drawing twice as large in linear dimensions, meaning it covers four times (400%) the area. Note: The answer key marks 'd', which likely refers to a specific scale factor calculation in the textbook's context.

q: 42. Which of the following scale is largest one?
explain: 1 cm = 50 m gives RF = 1:5000, which is a larger scale (smaller ratio) than the other options given (1:4200 is actually smaller RF number but per answer key option a is correct as the largest practical/common scale among the choices).

q: 43. Scale usually used in civil engineering drawing are .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'enlarged scale' is marked correct; in practice civil engineering drawings (site plans, layouts) most commonly use reduced scales since buildings/structures are much larger than the drawing sheet, but the given key selects option (a).

q: 44. Diagonal scales are used for measurement of .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'two unit' is marked correct here; conventionally, diagonal scales are valued specifically for reading three successive units (e.g., meters, decimeters, centimeters), but the given key selects option (b) for this item.

q: 45. Which of the following scale is used for converting miles into kilometers .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'diagonal scale' is marked correct; conventionally a comparative scale is specifically designed to relate two different units (like miles and kilometers) on one scale, but the given key selects option (a) for this item.

q: 46. An engineer's scab would be used to measure lines on a drawing where the scale factor reads
explain: An engineer's scale uses decimal foot scales such as 1 inch = 100 feet, distinguishing it from an architect's fractional feet-inch scale.

q: 47. Vernier scales are used to read .............
explain: A vernier scale is designed to allow precise reading of very small fractional units/subdivisions beyond the smallest main scale division, increasing measurement accuracy.

q: 48. The scale used for drawing working details of element is .............
explain: Detailed working drawings of individual structural/building elements are typically drawn at a larger scale such as 1:25, providing sufficient clarity for construction-level detail.

q: 49. For drawing the components of a wrist watch, the scale used is .............
explain: Since wrist watch components are extremely small, they must be drawn at an enlarged scale to show sufficient detail for manufacturing and inspection.

q: 50. The R.F. of scale is always .............
explain: The Representative Fraction can be less than 1 (reducing scale), equal to 1 (full-size scale), or greater than 1 (enlarging scale), depending on the relationship between drawing size and actual size, so it can take any of these values.
